title: After the phone's clock is moved back, the watch stops following the phone's workouts
what: The watch keeps the highest number the phone ever stamped on a rest or workout update and drops every later update with a smaller number. The phone makes that number from its clock. If the phone's clock was once ahead (set by hand to a later date or year, or wrong at first start) and is then corrected, every new rest, next set and workout update is thrown away on the watch until the clock passes the old time again, which can be days or years. Nothing on the watch ever clears the stored number.
expected: A correction of the phone's clock, a new phone or a reinstalled phone app never makes the watch ignore the phone; a much smaller number from the phone should be taken as a fresh start.
how_often: rare: only after the phone's clock was once set ahead
fix_line: Treat a phone number far below the stored one as a restart and accept it, or clear the stored number when the workout ends

items.reason: Fresh install catches up mid-workout from the phone's stored items; update re-arms a running rest and re-sends the watch version; old saved settings are carried over (old combined permission flag, pre-0.63 open workout); every newer phone field has a default, so mixed phone and watch versions work, and watch logging stays off with an older phone. Sideload phone and sideload watch share one signer; whether Play's app-signing key equals the sideload key (sideload phone with a Play watch) is data: unknown, not checkable from code. The panel-cache part does not apply to a watch app.

The watch has no trial, plan, gym-pause or staff logic: it shows only what the phone sends, and the gym colour follows each phone update (orange once the member has no gym). It uses elapsed times only, no calendar sums, so year end and leap day do not apply. Not opened for 6 months: an open workout older than 4 hours is dropped and an old rest is cleared. Owner changes phone: the watch never forgets it once saw the phone app (existing finding); a phone clock moved back makes the watch ignore the phone (new finding). Staff leaving does not apply: the watch is member-only.

New first-launch screens: watches that answered the old combined ask count as asked; the Alarms and reminders ask is shown once to updated watches too. A member who said Not now under the old ask never gets a way back (existing finding).
Updated watches have a path for each new ask, except a way back after Not now.
Rule applied: the one missing path is already a finding.
The watch has no What's new, dots or update notice. Its only tip (Tap a number, then turn the dial) shows to new and updated members alike on first sets, until used 3 times or shown on 10 exercises.
Rule applied: the tip also reaches members who logged on the watch before, but the dial itself changed in that same version, so it is not a new mark on an old thing. No fault.
